title: Incidence and Predictors of Meditation-Related Unusual Experiences and Adverse Effects in a Representative Sample of Meditators in the United States

cost.compute_notes: Abstract from the Crossref API (primary metadata). Data, materials and code reported at OSF 3mn9y, preregistration OSF r8beh -- OSF API answered 503 on 2026-10-17, not retrieved.

triggers: prevalence of meditation adverse effects depends on instrument
representative sample of US meditators adverse effects
Inventory of Meditation Experiences MRAES prevalence
meditation retreat participation predicts adverse effects

claims.statement: In a population-based survey of 886 US adults stratified by lifetime meditation experience, 96.6% reported an unusual experience, 58.4% an adverse effect (IME), 78.3% one or more MRAES items, 31.4% a challenging/difficult/distressing experience, and 9.1% functional impairment from adverse effects; distress, psychoticism, unusual beliefs and retreat participation predicted them.
claims.scope: Cross-sectional, US, approximately representative on age, gender, race/ethnicity; one sample, five instruments.

our_assessment.why: Abstract only. Worth recording now for one structural fact visible in the abstract itself: in ONE sample, 'prevalence of meditation adverse effects' runs from 9.1% to 96.6% depending on the instrument -- a tenfold range from definition alone. The single-item 'challenging/difficult/distressing' figure (31.4%) is the one comparable with the practitioner surveys' single items (schlosser2019 25.6%, cebolla2017 25.4%); the MRAES-any-item 78.3% is not. Retreat participation as a predictor agrees with schlosser2019 (OR 1.68). Data at OSF 3mn9y: retrieve when OSF is up, then read the paper and test the predictors.

relations.why: Retreat participation positively associated with adverse effects in both.
Single-item practitioner prevalence (25.4%) sits next to this sample's single-item 31.4%, not its instrument-based 58-97%.

open_questions: Retrieve OSF 3mn9y; read the full paper; is the retreat effect robust to the same adjustment schlosser2019 needed (years, type)?
Does any of the five instruments show the flat-in-years curve of schlosser2019 / the early rise of goldberg2022?
